sources.title: GTA 6 Launch Trailer Teases Jason's Troubled Past, a Steamy Shower Scene With Lucia, and Much More
sources.text: Rockstar has released the launch trailer for GTA 6 , which shows us brand new footage of Jason and Lucia as well as the open world. The trailer, which weighs in at 1:30, touches on Jason's troubled past, which involved leaving the army not on the best of terms. We see snippets of a steamy shower scene with Lucia, who is wearing an ankle tag, and plenty of explosive open-world action. Rather than showing gameplay, the launch trailer showcases cinematic action in GTA 6 as it nears its November 19 launch. As per Rockstar's partnership with Sony, the PS5 is prominent in the trailer, with the "plays best on PS5" message displayed at the start. The trailer confirms the footage was "captured on PS5." The trailer begins with some narration from Jason. "I got in some trouble in the army," he begins. "Didn't leave on the best of terms. They don't give loans or anything to people like me." We see a bearded Jason working at Brian's Marina, buffing a boat before he receives a call from Lucia Caminos. Presumably this is the call Jason gets to pick up Lucia from prison. We're shown what look like flashbacks to Jason's time in the army, where he appears to have been in the special forces. We see him wading through water as part of a military unit, and leaping out of a helicopter while on some sort of mission. But these scenes could easily be set in the "present," rather than the past, with Jason gearing up for, perhaps, a police operation. Either way, it explains why Jason is so handy with a gun. We're then treated to various shots showing Jason and Lucia getting up to no good across Vice City, with glimpses of that steamy shower scene. The shot of Lucia wearing an ankle tag could hint at initial restrictions to exploration, as more of the world is opened up during progression through the story, but that's speculation. This week, we learnt about GTA 6's sweat system, and there's a shot in the launch trailer that looks to show this in action. We see a man working out, and he's putting a lot of effort in. Sweat? Yep, it's all there. "Are we gonna be okay?" Lucia asks Jason after yet more explosive shots. "We stuck together through everything," Jason replies. "Just gotta get through it." Here's the official blurb from Rockstar on the GTA 6 launch trailer: We also have confirmation that electronic duo Justice composed the original score for GTA 6. Indeed their track, Flower in a Hurricane, featuring fellow Grammy-winners Tame Impala and SZA along with King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard, plays during the launch trailer. It's been a busy week for GTA 6. We've got a report on what sounds like the end of Cyberleek , details of GTA 6’s sweat system , and confirmation GTA 6 is eligible for The Game Awards 2026 . Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

sources.title: GTA 6's Official Launch Trailer Teases Wild Sex Scenes
sources.text: The short trailer from Rockstar shows the sights in Leonida, missions, and some steamier moments We are 35 days out from the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 , and Rockstar is drumming up hype for the game with an official launch trailer. The video provides a fresh look at the Florida-inspired state Leonida, as well as Jason and Lucia's story. It also features some, shall we say, heated moments between the two lovers . In the trailer, Jason receives a call from Lucia while in prison. He reveals he was discharged from the Army early for an unspecified reason. We get a look at a variety of heists, some of which can get surprisingly high-tech — Jason is shown wearing some gear that would look right at home in a Call of Duty game. The trailer is only a minute and a half long, but it also packs quick glimpses of intimate moments between Jason and Lucia. The two can be seen sharing a shower, kissing, and pushing each other up against the bathroom wall. It's here that the trailer reveals Lucia is still wearing an ankle monitor. It's not quite as risqué as the leaked footage of naked Lucia and Jason , but it's also not clear if playable portions of the game will actually mirror the leaks. In that unauthorized footage, Jason and Lucia walk around the city completely naked, with jiggle physics and everything, but the NPCs don't seem to remark on it. This has led some to speculate that the leaker was showing off nudity via dev tools. The game includes nudity, and game ratings say that GTA 6 will feature sex scenes . So far, it seems like the scenes are framed so players cannot see the characters' private parts. Rockstar has also revealed the trailer's soundtrack includes the debut of "Flower in a Hurricane," an original song by Justice. The original score features artists such as Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard. Rockstar previously gave players a taste of the open-world game's radio stations. GTA 6 will release on Nov. 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.

sources.title: GTA 6 launch trailer shows a more intimate Jason and Lucia as fans struggle to believe it's real
sources.text: New Grand Theft Auto 6 launch trailer really makes it feel real – we made it The GTA 6 launch trailer is here, formally ushering in the next era of Grand Theft Auto after more than a decade post-GTA 5. Rockstar shared the new trailer earlier today, "featuring the debut of 'Flower in a Hurricane' from original score composers Justice feat. Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard," and confirming that this song will appear on the official GTA 6 soundtrack album. The short trailer sees the dual protagonists, Jason and Lucia, open up about their struggles. Jason notably sports long hair for much of the trailer; in the opening seconds, he discusses the obstacles he's faced after a less-than-glamorous military departure. Lucia is seen sporting a monitoring anklet during an intimate shower scene, and at one point wonders, "Are we gonna be OK" amid a storm of crime. Rockstar was in a very helicopter mood with this trailer. One helicopter crashes behind an assault rifle-toting Jason, Lucia rides another through the streets with a grenade launcher in hand, and in a third sequence a chopper is shown carrying a chained load of (presumably stolen) cargo through the city like a wrecking ball, shattering a row of windows on another building. A once-again short-haired Jason emerges from a helicopter in the next shot, only to cut to him and Lucia jumping off a roof into some sort of hotel pool. "Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them," reads the video description. "But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive." The early response from Grand Theft Auto fans is unsurprisingly enormous, with millions piling into Rockstar's accounts across social media. The trailer crossed 1 million views on YouTube in about half an hour, if you can trust overwhelmed metrics. In the comments, GTA 6 hopefuls express disbelief at finally having a launch trailer in their hands. "I thought I would never live this moment," reads one top comment. "We are really at the finish line!!!" says another fan. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Grand Theft Auto 6 is out November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X. The launch trailer was captured on PS5, with a clear PlayStation marketing push bookending it. As if you needed another reminder of why GTA 6 took so long, it has a realistic sweat system that makes Jason and Lucia perspire based on how hard they dance . He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible. sources.text: Dino Crisis 2 e RollerCoaster Tycoon 3 Complete Edition chegam no PlayStation Plus Deluxe. Neste mês, mergulhe no submundo do crime da Sicília do início do século XX em Mafia: The Old Country, enfrente uma fronteira mortal repleta de máquinas impressionantes em Horizon Forbidden West ou encare hordas de inimigos fúngicos com um arsenal extravagante de armas futuristas no jogo de ação cooperativa frenética Mycopunk, todos chegam no catálogo de jogos do PlayStation Plus já em outubro. Enquanto isso, o PlayStation Plus Premium recebe Dino Crisis 2 e RollerCoaster Tycoon 3. A lista completa de títulos estará disponível para jogar em 20 de outubro, salvo indicação em contrário. E, com a chegada da temporada de Halloween, os membros da PlayStation Plus podem aproveitar uma seleção de ofertas exclusivas como parte das nossas comemorações do Horrorfest. Confira os detalhes completos abaixo desta publicação. Descubra as origens do crime organizado nesta conturbada história de máfia ambientada no submundo brutal da Sicília do início do século XX. Lute para sobreviver como Enzo Favara e prove seu valor para a família nesta envolvente ação em terceira pessoa, que se passa em um momento histórico perigoso e implacável. Esta fantástica história ganha ainda mais vida com os visuais impressionantes, a narrativa cinematográfica e o realismo autêntico que consagrou a fama da aclamada série Mafia. A história de Enzo se passa em uma época em que a destreza com uma lâmina de estilete era letal, a espingarda lupara de cano cerrado era a arma de fogo preferida, vinganças sangrentas se prolongaram por décadas e os mafiosos patrulhavam seus territórios a pé, a cavalo ou ao volante dos primeiros automóveis. Acompanhe Aloy ao enfrentar o Oeste Proibido em uma fronteira majestosa, mas perigosa, que esconde novas e misteriosas ameaças. Explore terras distantes, enfrente máquinas maiores e mais imponentes e conheça novas tribos extraordinárias neste retorno ao futuro distante e pós-apocalíptico de Horizon. Reencontre velhos amigos, firme alianças com novas facções em conflito e desvende o legado de um passado ancestral — tudo isso enquanto tenta manter-se um passo à frente de um novo inimigo aparentemente invencível. Fatie alienígenas fúngicos neste jogo de tiro com saque baseado em missões e com altíssimo nível de personalização. Centenas de melhorias feitas à mão, modo cooperativo para 4 jogadores e um pequeno homem-barata. Como não amar? Um esquadrão de robôs rejeitados é contratado pela corporação SAXON e recebe uma última chance de conquistar a glória e alguns lucros (e evitar o ferro-velho). É a Equipe de Risco de Novo Atlas, um esquadrão de exterminadores em frangalhos enviado para descobrir os mistérios por trás de uma catástrofe fúngica que afeta todo o planeta. Embarque numa série de missões perigosas no planeta para afastar a ameaça micológica. Será um simples desastre natural como alegam? E será que a SAXON não fez direito a sua declaração de imposto de renda? Ou foi culpa sua? Mycopunk chega ao Catálogo de Jogos PlayStation dia 20 de outubro. Após um confronto com Huggy Wuggy e libertar Poppy, você deve descer mais fundo na fábrica de brinquedos da Playtime Co. Quebra-cabeças desafiadores e brinquedos horripilantes aguardam. Use ganchos, balance-se e abra caminho com força até a segurança. Tente escapar, e não deixe a mamãe encontrar você. Continue explorando as profundezas da Playtime Co. em busca de respostas. Sua jornada para descobrir o que aconteceu dentro da fábrica está apenas começando… Poppy Playtime: Chapter 2 estará disponível em 27 de outubro. Embarque em The Midnight Walk, uma aventura de fantasia sombria e reverente moldada em argila, criada pelas mentes por trás de Lost in Random, Fe e Ghost Giant. Torne-se o The Burnt One, faça amizade com uma criatura-lanterna perdida chamada Potboy e use a chama dele para iluminar seu caminho por um mundo de contrastes, repleto de maravilhas e horrores. Sobreviva e supere com astúcia os muitos monstros ávidos por devorar a chama do seu amiguinho enquanto vivencia cinco contos de fogo e escuridão, com um elenco incrível de personagens peculiares. Encante-se com cada detalhe perturbador de uma paisagem meticulosamente criada à mão com argila real e animada no estilo stop-motion. Totalmente jogável tanto no PS5 quanto em RV – com o PS VR2. The Midnight Walk estará disponível hoje, 14 de outubro. Tales of Arise – Beyond the Dawn Edition | PS5, PS4 Por 300 anos, Rena dominou Dahna, saqueando os recursos de seu planeta e privando as pessoas de sua dignidade e liberdade. Nossa história começa com duas pessoas nascidas em mundos diferentes, cada uma procurando mudar seu destino e criar um novo futuro. Com um elenco diversificado de personagens, um sistema de combate intuitivo e gratificante e uma história cativante ambientada em um exuberante mundo pelo qual vale a pena lutar, Tales of Arise oferece uma experiência de JRPG excelente. Tales of Arise – Beyond the Dawn Edition estará disponível em 27 de outubro. Monster Energy Supercross 25 – The Official Video Game | PS5 Vivencie a emoção de correr em pistas recém-projetadas que replicam eventos do mundo real e dispute com a mais recente lista de pilotos profissionais: abra o caminho em uma carreira renovada com competições intensas, rivalidades e escolhas estratégicas. Graças ao Unreal Engine 5, aproveite um gameplay renovado com física realista e evolução dinâmica da pista, tornando cada volta única e desafiadora. Domine o fluxo com tutoriais abertos, uma wiki abrangente e assistência de pilotagem da Neural Technology. Monster Energy Supercross 25 – The Official Video estará disponível em 27 de outubro. stories.title: Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser says he 'failed' with Max Payne 3, and I'm sorry Danno but that's just plain wrong

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser says he 'failed' with Max Payne 3, and I'm sorry Danno but that's just plain wrong
sources.text: Dan Houser is a co-founder of Rockstar Games and so I would never presume to tell him he's wrong about any of the games Rockstar has made— except in this one particular instance, where I feel obligated to step up and say, 'Dan, I'm sorry bud, but you're wrong.' The game in question is Max Payne 3 , on which Houser played a central role, and one he seems rather down on: In an interview with IGN , he said the game was a "failure" because, simply put, he's not Sam Lake, the Remedy creative director who wrote the first two Max Payne games. As a very linear game, Max Payne 3 "was a little different" from the open world GTA games he was accustomed to, Houser said, but he also really enjoyed the experience. "I loved what we did design-wise, the way the game didn't have loads, the way it felt like a 12-hour movie, some of the visual stuff we did with words on screen. Alas, he continued, "I felt we were creating a really cool digital noir experience, and the consensus at the time was that people hated it. "So I got that completely wrong," Houser said. "I know Sam Lake well, and he's a very good guy and really talented. I thought we'd done a good job of doing another Max Payne game. Some people liked it; lots didn't. So we got it wrong, or I got it wrong. I failed. My bit was not a success. "The game is beautifully made, and it wasn't as successful as it should have been. So I would say a large amount of that failure was on me as one of the people making the decisions and also as the writer, when people really missed his writing." Max Payne 3 is a really interesting case study because it's very much a Max Payne game—grim and gritty, filled with bullet time, body drops, and snappy commentary about how much life sucks—but it's also a full-on Rockstar game, and thus a very different vibe from the previous two entries in the series. Fans who were expecting more of the same—or insisting on it, really—were bound to be disappointed. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. But Max Payne 3 itself is nothing short of a brilliant, powerhouse cinematic shooter. It really does feel like "a 12-hour movie," powered by lush cut scenes, a brilliant soundtrack by industrial rock group Health, and great performances across the board, in particular from James McCaffrey in the title role. With all due respect to Remedy, this is where McCaffrey really hit his stride, digging deep to deliver some truly great lines: It is fair to say that Max Payne 3 wasn't a massive commercial success: In 2012, publisher Take-Two Interactive said sales of the game came in " lower than expected ," resulting in a significantly increased net loss for the quarter. But that's hardly the only measure of success, and I think it's notable that Take-Two said the same, at the same time, about Spec Ops: The Line , a game widely heralded, then and now, for its daring, subversive narrative. Max Payne 3 was a slower burn, but I think the passage of time has given us a far better perspective on what Rockstar actually delivered: As former PC Gamer writer Andy Kelly wrote a full decade ago, "Over the years I’ve developed a greater appreciation for the risks Rockstar took in breaking Remedy’s established, and beloved, mould." "It’s a radical departure, but it works," the other Andy wrote in his very correct take on Max Payne 3 . "It’s always interesting to see a familiar character thrust into an unfamiliar situation, and Max is hilariously out of place in Brazil. As if being a white American in a favela didn’t draw enough unwanted attention, he makes his life even more difficult by wearing the loudest Hawaiian shirt imaginable. He was comfortable in New York, but here he’s an outsider, and the game plays up to it brilliantly." And so, Dan, with all due respect, I have to say, 'I'm sorry bud, but you're wrong.' Max Payne 3 may have been divisive in its time, and it may not have been the big hit you were hoping for, but I sure wouldn't call it a failure. I'd say Rockstar, and you, absolutely nailed it. Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. sources.title: Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser blames himself for Max Payne 3 - "a large amount of that failure was on me"
sources.text: "The consensus at the time was that people hated it." Max Payne 3 is a bit of a strange project. Unlike its two predecessors, the game wasn't developed by original creator Remedy Entertainment, rather it was the product of Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption studio Rockstar Games . Despite that pedigree, it is seen as something of a failure - or, at least, not quite what fans wanted from the third game in the iconic third-person shooter series. And Dan Houser, co-founder of Rockstar, says it was his fault. In a wide-ranging interview with IGN , Houser, who was also Max Payne 3's lead writer, recalled his experience working on the game and how it differed from other Rockstar projects. "It was a linear game, so it was a little different from writing an open-world game, a little more structured," Houser said. "I really enjoyed that as an experience. I loved what we did design-wise, the way the game didn't have loads, the way it felt like a 12-hour movie, some of the visual stuff we did with words on screen. I felt we were creating a really cool digital noir experience, and the consensus at the time was that people hated it." Houser is being a little harsh here; Max Payne 3 was critically acclaimed at launch . The same stylistic, tonal and visual choices many didn't like are what also set it apart from the two prior games. Indeed, Max Payne 3's mechanics remain among the series' best to this day, with smooth third-person movement and sharp gunplay that make it a joy to play over 14 years later. "I know Sam Lake [creator of Max Payne ] well, and he's a very good guy and really talented. I thought we'd done a good job of doing another Max Payne game," Houser added. "Some people liked it; lots didn't. So we got it wrong, or I got it wrong. I failed. My bit was not a success." Max Payne 3 is seen as a commercial disappointment by publisher Take-Two, who said its "lower than expected sales" were mainly responsible for a loss of $110m (~£82,9m) that financial quarter . Houser acknowledged the lower sales in the interview, saying "it wasn't as successful as it should have been". "So I would say a large amount of that failure was on me as one of the people making the decisions and also as the writer, when people really missed [Sam Lake]'s writing," Houser added. Years after Max Payne 3's release, Remedy and Rockstar would be reunited on a mega-project: a remake of Max Payne 1 and 2, which Remedy said two years ago had entered full production . It is understood the remake is Remedy's next project.

sources.title: Max Payne 3 “Failed,” According to Rockstar Games Co-Founder
sources.text: Remedy Entertainment sold the rights to Max Payne to Rockstar Games, which had a grand vision for the third game. Max Payne 3 was released, sold millions, and earned the praise of many. But Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser believes Max Payne 3 got some things wrong. The upcoming Max Payne remakes have Remedy back at the helm and are being developed with Rockstar Games. The latter took over the franchise with the third mainline game, and Dan Houser, who’s making more media appearances than ever this year, explained why he isn’t as high on Max Payne 3 . In an interview with IGN , Houser, who has since founded Absurd Ventures, talked about Max Payne 3, Rockstar’s involvement with the game, and ultimately why he thought “the consensus at the time was that people hated it.” “So I got that completely wrong. I know Sam Lake well, and he’s a very good guy and really talented. I thought we’d done a good job of doing another Max Payne game. Some people liked it; lots didn’t. So we got it wrong, or I got it wrong. I failed. My bit was not a success. The game is beautifully made, and it wasn’t as successful as it should have been. So I would say a large amount of that failure was on me as one of the people making the decisions and also as the writer, when people really missed his writing.” “It was a linear game, so it was a little different from writing an open-world game, a little more structured. I really enjoyed that as an experience. I loved what we did design-wise, the way the game didn’t have loads, the way it felt like a 12-hour movie, some of the visual stuff we did with words on screen. I felt we were creating a really cool digital noir experience, and the consensus at the time was that people hated it. Max Payne 3 has shipped over four million copies and is rated critically alongside the first two games. Is Houser being too harsh on himself? sources.title: 007 First Light for Switch 2 launches March 18, 2027
sources.text: The Switch 2 version of 007 First Light will launch on March 18, 2027, developer IO Interactive announced. Pre-orders are available now. 007 First Light first launched for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, and PC via Steam and Epic Games Store on May 27, 2026. Here is an overview of the game, via IO Interactive: Follow James Bond as a young, resourceful and sometimes reckless recruit in MI6’s training program, and discover an origin story of the world’s most famous spy. After a heroic act, young Naval air crewman James Bond is offered to join the newly revived Double 0 program. But when a mission to stop a rogue agent ends in tragedy, he must join forces with his reluctant mentor Greenway to expose a deep conspiracy and stop a looming coup at the heart of the State.

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: 007 First Light gets Switch 2 release date, with IO Interactive saying time for "optimisation and performance" was needed
sources.text: The Switch 2 version of 007 First Light will be released 18th March, 2027, IO Interactive has announced. The game had originally been expected this summer but IOI announced a delay to an unspecific date in March roughly a month ago. "Since announcing additional development time to ensure the quality of experience players expect, IO Interactive has brought hands-on builds of 007 First Light to both gamescom and Tokyo Game Show, where players and press had their first opportunity to experience Bond's world running on Nintendo's hardware," the company said in a press release statement. "Player response from both events has been positive, reflecting the progress being made across the game as development continues toward launch. The development team will use the coming months to continue refining the game's optimisation and performance on Nintendo Switch 2, ensuring it meets the standard players expect at launch." Evidently, it hasn't been a smooth transition. We've heard similar things from Capcom, for what it's worth, with the Monster Hunter Wilds devs claiming it was a "painstaking, seemingly endless process" to get the game running well on Switch 2. The date announcement coincides with pre-orders of a Deluxe Edition going live, which offers access to some extra clothes and gadgets in game. We're also only a couple of weeks on from 007 First Light getting a bumper blob of add-on content , in the form of New Game Plus, a new, harder difficulty, a photo mode, more replayable TacSim challenge missions, and a bit of general game tuning. Presumably all of this will be included in the Switch 2 version when it launches. As it stands, 007 First Light has been one of the stand-out successes of 2026, bringing James Bond back to gaming with flair and aplomb. The Hitman studio delivered a tight, exciting, cinematic single-player adventure filled with charm and wit - not unlike James Bond himself. Eurogamer's gleaming 007 First Light review can tell you more. The game also appears to have been a commercial success, having passed 4 million sales since release - and with a Switch 2 version to come, there's more selling to do. I imagine it makes the likelihood of a sequel very strong, though newish Bond franchise owner Amazon has said it wants to be involved in whatever comes next , whereas IOI was the master of its own destiny with 007 First Light. Meanwhile, IOI is also making a fantasy game called, well, Project Fantasy. This was announced as an online RPG in 2023 , but faced a major setback recently when publisher Xbox pulled out of the project , forcing IOI to close one of its studios and make layoffs across the company - even in the aftermath of 007 First LIght's success. IOI has since regained full ownership of the game and has vowed to continue to develop Project Fantasy independently . The studio also continues to develop and expand Hitman World of Assassination, which recently added rapper Snoop Dogg as an elusive target .

sources.title: Big Walk Developer Explains Why the Game Isn't on Xbox
sources.text: Big Walk developer House House has explained why it’s boycotting Xbox and thus why the game isn’t available on Microsoft's console. House House, the Australian studio behind Untitled Goose Game, released clever co-op puzzle adventure Big Walk earlier this year on PC, PlayStation 5, and Nintendo Switch 2, leaving Xbox Series X and S out in the cold. Big Walk was critically acclaimed upon release, earning a 91 rating on Metacritic and multiple appearances on Game of the Year contender lists. IGN’s Big Walk review returned a 9/10. We said: “Big Walk is a rewarding co-op adventure full of beautiful emergent moments as you find solutions to cleverly built puzzles and explore its vast open world with your friends.” Since then, fans had wondered why the game failed to come out Xbox. In a statement published to its website , House House said it made the decision as part of its support for campaign group Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS), which describes itself as a “Palestinian-led movement for freedom, justice and equality.” BDS lists Xbox as a “priority” target, and has launched a campaign calling on gamers, streamers, and developers to boycott Microsoft’s gaming efforts. As reported by the BBC , Microsoft's work with the Israeli government has been a controversial issue, including within the company itself, prompting protests by some employees. House House indicated that it won't release Big Walk on Xbox "until Microsoft and/or Xbox have been removed as BDS boycott targets." sources.text: "Meaningful change can be made in the world". Big Walk developer House House has explained the lack of an Xbox version for the popular co-operative puzzle game, pointing to the ongoing BDS boycott as the core reason behind its decision. In a post made to House House social media accounts , the team writes: "It has always been our intention for Big Walk to be played by groups of friends, and we know that keeping the game off Xbox runs counter to those intentions. This decision means that some people will miss out on playing Big Walk with their friends, and we understand the disappointment we’re causing. We are disappointed too. "We would love for people to be able to play the game on Xbox, but not until Microsoft and/or Xbox have been removed as BDS boycott targets. "We’ve made this decision with the belief that meaningful change can be made in the world, that coordinated collective action can confront even the most powerful interests, and that one day, Palestine will be free." The Palestinian-led BDS movement has been a staunch proponent of various boycotts aimed at companies who have supported Israel's government during the genocide in Palistine. It has published a list of boycott targets, which includes Disney, Intel, and Xbox. Xbox's inclusion on the list is due to Microsoft's partnership with Israel and its prison system according to BDS. BDS has urged people to cancel their Game Pass subscriptions, boycott major franchises including Call of Duty and Candy Crush , and cease purchases of Microsoft gaming products. stories.title: Estúdio brasileiro comemora lançamento de Deep Dish Dungeon no Game Pass: “É um privilégio para nós”
stories.summary: The post Estúdio brasileiro comemora lançamento de Deep Dish Dungeon no Game Pass: “É um privilégio para nós” appeared first on Xbox Wire em Português .

sources.name: Xbox Wire BR
sources.title: Estúdio brasileiro comemora lançamento de Deep Dish Dungeon no Game Pass: “É um privilégio para nós”
sources.text: Saulo Camarotti estava explorando uma masmorra no famoso jogo de sobrevivência Valheim quando teve uma ideia: “Essa dungeon sozinha poderia ser um jogo muito legal”, ele relembra em uma conversa com o XBOX Wire. Dois anos depois, esse jogo se tornou real e está sendo lançado como Deep Dish Dungeons no XBOX Series X|S hoje, 13 de outubro, e disponível desde o primeiro dia para assinantes de XBOX Game Pass Ultimate. Em antecipação à chegada de mais um jogo brasileiro ao Game Pass, conversamos com Saulo para explorarmos juntos essa masmorra de Deep Dish Dungeon , talvez até encontrar alguns segredos…. Gênero : Dungeon Crawler/Survivor/Metroidvania Desenvolvedora : Behold Studios Publicadora : Raw Fury Plataformas : Steam, XBOX Series X|S, XBOX no PC e Portátil Modos : solo ou multiplayer até 3 jogadores online Funcionalidades : XBOX Play Anywhere e Cross-Play (Steam e consoles XBOX) Idioma : português Brasileiro nas legendas e interface Em Deep Dish Dungeon controlamos um explorador em busca de tesouros em uma masmorra, sozinho ou na companhia de amigos. E é isso. Uma premissa simples e sem muitos rodeios, já que a ideia, segundo Saulo, nunca foi guiar o jogador para onde ele deve ir. “Eu queria criar uma experiência sobre explorar uma masmorra como um aventureiro e não como um guerreiro”, explica o desenvolvedor. “Não é sobre matar, morrer e ganhar nível. Esse é um jogo em que você tenta entender esse lugar antigo em ruinas e tenta sobreviver”. Com esse foco em exploração, Saulo diz que Deep Dish Dungeon tem uma média de 15 horas de duração até ser finalizado. Enquanto o jogador descobre mais sobre o tesouro que está buscando, e o próprio lugar em si por meio de narrativas espalhadas pelo cenário, surge uma das mecânicas de jogos mais importantes: cozinhar. Já dizia o ditado: saco vazio não para em pé… nem explora, por isso que é fundamental preparar comidas que dão vantagens ao jogador – daí o “Dish” (prato de comida em tradução livre) no nome. “Você come antes de se aventurar. Não é depois, para se curar”, explica Saulo. “E cada categoria de ingrediente no jogo dá uma vantagem diferente, como mais vida ou vigor”. Foi nesse aspecto da culinária que a Behold colocou um tempero de brasilidade ao jogo, com ingredientes como semente de guaraná e mandioca (ou macaxeira ou aipim dependendo da região do país) ou quitutes como coxinha , pastel e bolo de fubá que podem ser preparados. Dá até água na boca. Alguns exemplos de efeito de ingredientes: A própria presença desses ingredientes típicos do Brasil também dá dicas da localização dessa masmorra, apesar do jogo nunca revelar de fato onde é. “O jogo acontece num lugar fictício, mas para nós, internamente, está mais ou menos ali na Amazônia”, revela Saulo. A partir desse conceito, o time se baseou nas criações de elementos de arte e arquitetura que compõe o lugar. Outra caraterística importante em Deep Dish Dungeons é que masmorra que o jogador explora é fixa e não criada proceduralmente. Saulo diz que isso foi uma decisão proposital. Para que cada lugar, obstáculo e segredo foi pensado para dar um senso de progressão que é mais próximo dos jogos no estilo “Metroidvania” do que os de Survival. “A masmorra é toda interconectada que nem um Metroidvania, e à medida que você encontra ferramentas e ganha habilidades, você consegue abrir novas salas e explorar mais a fundo”, explica o desenvolvedor. Essas ferramentas podem ser achadas pelo cenário ou criadas com recurso coletados durante a exploração. Ao obter um martelo , por exemplo, é possível quebrar portas de ferro que antes bloqueavam uma nova área. Já criar um gancho abre possibilidades de agora ir a lugares elevados que podem ter passagens secretas ou dar acesso a novos ambientes. Deep Dish Dungeon é o primeiro título da Behold Studios a chegar no XBOX Game Pass. No Brasil, o estúdio ganhou notoriedade na década passada ao lançar sucessos indies como Knights of Pen & Papper e Chroma Squad , mas Saulo diz que o novo jogo representa uma nova fase para eles, de projetos com produções rápidas e de escopo simples, mas eficaz. O novo game foi desenvolvido em apenas dois anos e por uma equipe de duas pessoas: Saulo na direção, programação e Game Design, e Carolina Baumgarten na arte. Por isso, a visibilidade dada pelo Game Pass foi o estímulo muito bem-vindo para o estúdio nesse momento, como a refeição que dá benefícios antes da exploração da masmorra, ou nessa, caso, do lançamento do jogo. Saulo também explica que estar no Game Pass impulsiona um dos aspectos mais importantes de Deep Dish Dungeon : o multiplayer. Apesar de poder ser jogado sozinho, o jogo foi pensado, desde o início, para ser uma experiência compartilhada junto com outras pessoas em cooperação. “Criar uma comunidade multiplayer nesse tipo de jogo é essencial”, diz Saulo. ““O nosso jogo é multiplayer e cross-play. Então, se você está jogando no Game Pass, pode chamar um amigo que tá no Steam”. Então, reúna seus amigos exploradores, estejam eles no console ou no PC, prepare os suplementos, cozinhe um bolo de fubá e saia para descobrir os segredos e tesouros de Deep Dish Dungeon , que já está disponível exclusivamente nos consoles para XBOX Series X|S, XBOX no PC e no XBOX Game Pass Ultimate.

sources.title: Valor Mortis: Tips and Tricks to Survive the Crimson Plague
sources.text: The Crimson Plague is ravaging Europe. Scattered across every level, echoes of the fallen and journal pages reveal the army’s secrets and the horrors of the plague. In Valor Mortis , you play William, a young Englishman disillusioned with the monarchy who joins Napoleon’s cause, drawn by the promise of a unified Europe. He dies for that ideal — and you’ll need every tool at your disposal to survive what follows in Valor Mortis , available today for XBOX Series X|S, XBOX on PC, Game Pass, and with support for XBOX Play Anywhere. Before you lead William into battle, the team at One More Level wants to share how its combat really works, and a few things we hope you will go looking for. Valor Mortis is a soulslike, but its systems are built to feed each other. Your blade breaks posture. Your firearms hit weak points. Hitting weak points refills your nephtoglobin (nephto), and killing enemies often drops ammo. Once that loop clicks, you are always one move away from your next advantage. Ambers are where your build gets personal. Some simply make you stronger, but the best ones change how the game plays. Slot them in when you visit a lantern. The more you level William, the more Ambers you can equip, so use catalyst clots from your inventory to push past the next level threshold. Here are three that show how far an Amber can take your build: Every major boss has a strategy that works best against it. If a fight isn’t going your way, try different Transmutations, firearm combinations, and items from your inventory, and come back with a new plan. Valor Mortis rewards you for exploring, like a metroidvania. Abilities you unlock later open up areas you have already visited. Later levels open into combat arenas with fights across multiple heights, and villages are full of shortcuts and alternate paths. The best rewards are off the main path. Echoes of the fallen and journal pages fill in the story of the Crimson Plague. Many Ambers are tucked into optional areas, and you are unlikely to find every one of them in a single playthrough. Some of the most powerful enemies in Valor Mortis are also the best hidden. Optional mini-bosses wait in the corners of its interconnected levels for players curious enough to look. You never know what you will discover, or what kind of trouble you will find. Valor Mortis is available today for XBOX Series X|S, XBOX on PC, Game Pass, and with support for XBOX Play Anywhere. We can’t wait to see the builds you create and the secrets you uncover.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: GTA 6's Level of Detail Is So Extreme, Rockstar Built an Entire Scripted System Just for Sweat
sources.text: Rockstar Games is of course known for its attention to detail, with previous Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption games raising the bar for realism. GTA 6 , though, looks set to go further than any video game before it, with a dedicated system that determines how much the characters sweat. Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier said in a new video accompaniment to his making of GTA 6 article published this week, that Rockstar told him of a scripted system in the game that makes dual protagonists Jason and Lucia — or, it sounds like, any character in the game — exert different amounts of sweat depending on how much effort they’re putting into whatever activity they’re doing. So, in a nightclub, for example, Lucia will sweat more if she’s putting a lot of effort into dancing. Similarly, the harder Jason works out, the more he’ll sweat. We might have already seen GTA 6's sweat system in action. In the Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look video released in August, we briefly see Lucia dancing in a nightclub, and there's a distinct glisten to her skin that suggests she's sweating. Or maybe it's a trick of the light. This shows the incredible level of detail in GTA 6 — above and beyond any video game ever made — but it also helps explain why GTA 6 took so long to develop (eight years in terms of proper development work), and why it cost so much money to make ( not more than $1.5 billion, but no doubt the most expensive video game of all time ). Indeed, as the Bloomberg article reveals, Rockstar set up a new studio in Los Angeles packed with writers, producers, and directors, just to make NPCs. GTA 6 has suffered a number of high-profile delays, each of which has been explained publicly as part of Rockstar’s mission to achieve video game perfection with this game. When you hear about the sweat that’s poured into it, you start to understand what this will actually look like when the game itself comes out. With GTA 6 out next month, we’ve got plenty more for you to sink your teeth into, including our in-depth interview with Rockstar North's Rob Nelson in full, our report on what sounds like the end of Cyberleek , and some of the unusual marketing rockstar has put in place. sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: When Rockstar Needed To Delay GTA 6 Again, Take-Two’s CEO Replied: ‘Please Tell Me You’re Kidding’
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 GTA 6 Rockstar Games Strauss Zelnick In May 2025, Rockstar announced it was delaying Grand Theft Auto 6 until May 2026. Then, a few months later, it announced it was delaying GTA 6 again to November 2026 . For many fans, these back-to-back delays were excruciating and disappointing. And for Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, it apparently seemed like a prank. On October 14, Bloomberg published a lengthy report about Rockstar Games and its work on GTA 6 , its upcoming open-world crime simulator that is set to be the biggest game release of the decade when it arrives on November 19. However, remember that when the game was first revealed in December 2023, Rockstar promised a launch window of 2025. According to Rockstar’s leaders, they believed that was possible, though some devs below them weren’t convinced.
